correctness.rationale: For invertible A and Euclidean surface-area measure on ∂(AB²ᵈ), Jacobian is |det A| ||A⁻¹u|| (orthogonal/diagonal reduction), while volume covariance is A²/(d+2). The Gaussian identity ||A⁻¹u||=√(π/2) E_G |⟨A⁻¹G,u⟩| plus spherical |⟨z,u⟩|-weighted second moments yields Σ_surface=A(I+Q)A/(d+1), Q=E[ZZᵀ/||Z||]/E||Z||, Z=A⁻¹G. Matrix Q positive definite, diagonal q_i>0 sum1, hence strict Loewner lower bound. A symmetric strictly log-convex mean norm Φ(log 1/a_i) has gradient q_i and implies q_i oppositely ordered to a_i²; reverse Chebyshev gives ∑a_i²q_i≤(∑a_i²)/d, ball-only equality and sharp ratio upper (d+2)/d. Flat family axes (ε,1,…,1) has q_long≤ε and infimum (d+2)/(d+1), not attained. Independently integrated 100,000 angular points for planar ellipses axes (1,1),(.7,1),(.1,1),(.003,1): ratios ≈2,1.94030,1.38135,1.33342, consistent with d=2 sharp [4/3,2]. The analytic proof, not finite quadrature, supplies all-d assertions.
